problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize F=f+ψ over a convex set Q. The differentiable function f is convex on the entire ambient space, and ψ is convex on Q. A minimizer exists; strong convexity is not required.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CompositeGeneralizedSmooth.lean: objective; spec.admissible convexity and minimizer clauses.

problem_class.label: composite
problem_class.details: The objective combines a continuously differentiable convex component f with a potentially nonsmooth convex component ψ and the constraint x∈Q.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: A gradient query at any x returns ∇f(x) exactly, independently of the call index and oracle seed. No function-value oracle is supplied.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CompositeGeneralizedSmooth.lean: Query.gradient; spec.admissible gradient-answer and HasGradientAt clauses.

oracle.label: proximal
oracle.details: For every a>0 and z,v, an exact proximal query returns a minimizer over Q of ‖u−z‖²/(2a)+⟨v,u−z⟩+ψ(u). Each gradient or proximal query counts as one oracle call within a fixed budget.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CompositeGeneralizedSmooth.lean: Query.prox; proxObjective; spec.admissible proximal clauses. LongTails/Template.lean: execute; Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: L0>0 and L1≥0. For any segment [x,y] on which ‖∇f‖≤M, ‖∇f(x)−∇f(y)‖≤(L0+L1M)‖x−y‖. The gradient is continuous; twice differentiability and global Lipschitz continuity of the gradient are not assumed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is an arbitrary real Hilbert space. Public information comprises E,L0,L1,R,Δ,x0, with R,Δ>0. Some minimizer x⋆ satisfies ‖x0−x⋆‖≤R, F(x0)−F(x⋆)≤Δ, and ‖∇f(x⋆)‖≤G, where G≥0 may be nonzero. G and ε>0 are hidden from algorithm construction; neither Q nor ψ is supplied explicitly as public input.

setup_category.reason: Composite convex proximal optimization is standard, but this formulation uses gradient-dependent segment smoothness in an arbitrary Hilbert space, permits a nonzero smooth-component gradient at a composite minimizer, and hides G and ε from algorithm construction.

descriptionHtml:
Composite Generalized Smooth Minimization

We consider minimizing F=f+ψ over a convex set Q in a real Hilbert space E, where f,ψ:E→R. The function f is convex and continuously differentiable, ψ is convex on Q, and f is (L0,L1)-smooth with L0>0 and L1≥0. A given point x0∈Q has bounded distance and objective gap to a minimizer x⋆, whose gradient norm is bounded. The oracle returns ∇f(x) at x and exact constrained proximal minimizers. For ε>0, the goal is x¯∈Q with F(x¯)−F(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈QF(x),F(x):=f(x)+ψ(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ on E. The parameters satisfy L0>0,L1≥0,R>0,Δ>0,G≥0,ε>0. The algorithm receives only E,L0,L1,R,Δ, and x0; G and ε may enter the oracle-call budget but are not algorithm inputs.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity). The set Q⊆E is convex. For every t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y)for x,y∈E,ψ((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)ψ(x)+tψ(y)for x,y∈Q.

Assumption 2 (Generalized smoothness). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere on E, and ∇f:E→E is continuous. For every x,y∈E and M∈R, the implication ∥∇f(x+θ(y−x))∥≤Mfor every θ∈[0,1]⟹∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤(L0+L1M)∥x−y∥ holds.

Assumption 3 (Exact proximal access). There is a map T:R×E×E→E such that, for every a>0 and z,v∈E, T(a,z,v)∈argminu∈Q{∥u−z∥22a+⟨v,u−z⟩+ψ(u)}.

Assumption 4 (Initialization and minimizer bounds). The given starting point satisfies x0∈Q. There exists x⋆∈Q such that F(x⋆)≤F(x)for every x∈Q,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R,F(x0)−F(x⋆)≤Δ,∥∇f(x⋆)∥≤G.

The oracle returns ∇f(x) at x. It also accepts a proximal query (a,z,v)∈R×E×E and returns T(a,z,v); the minimization property is required for a>0. Gradient queries may be made at any x∈E. Gradient and proximal queries each count as one call toward a shared oracle-call budget.

After the allotted calls, the output must satisfy x¯∈Q,F(x¯)−F(x⋆)≤εP-a.s.

comparisonHtml:
Minimize F=f+ψ over convex Q in a real Hilbert space. The function f is convex and continuously differentiable on the whole space, with ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤(L0+L1M)∥x−y∥ whenever ∥∇f∥≤M on [x,y]; ψ is convex on Q, and exact gradient and proximal queries are available. Here L0,R,Δ,ε>0, L1,G≥0, x0∈Q, and some minimizer x⋆∈Q satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R, F(x0)−F(x⋆)≤Δ, and ∥∇f(x⋆)∥≤G. Target: a feasible output x with F(x)−F(x⋆)≤ε, deterministically.

Accelerated composite optimization under generalized smoothness: CompositeGeneralizedSmooth.

(2) (Tyurin 2026), Thm. 4.3. Special case: Q=Rd, ψ=0, G=0; twice differentiable f; R=∥x0−x⋆∥. O(1+L0R2ε+L1Rlog+(min{L12ΔL0,Δε})+log+ΔL0R2) gradient calls; R¯=R, Γ0=2Δ/R2. (1): Scope extends acceleration to constrained/composite objectives with ∇f(x⋆)≠0. Matches the leading rate on the overlap, up to logarithmic terms. (1): Larger logarithmic term can occur when L1>0, ε>L0/L12; worse leading constant on the overlap.
(3) AC-FGM (Li and Lan 2024), Cor. 1 and local-smoothness remark. Finite-dimensional, closed Q and closed convex ψ. O(1+L¯(R2+d12)ε) gradient, value and prox calls in total; arbitrary initial η1>0, fixed β=1/10. (1): No function values; explicit accelerated composite bound in setup parameters. Rates are not comparable through an unspecified trajectory curvature L¯. (1): Needs L0,L1,R,Δ for updates and G for its stopping budget; (3) has parameter-free updates.

Abbr: Each gradient, value or prox evaluation counts as one call. A prox query minimizes ∥u−z∥2/(2a)+⟨v,u−z⟩+ψ(u) over u∈Q, a>0. log+⁡t=max{0,log⁡t} for t>0, with log+⁡0=0. In (3), z0=x0, d1=∥z1−z0∥, and L¯=supt≥1max{[4(1−β)η1]−1,ℓ1,…,ℓt}; ℓt are the curvature estimates in Eqs. (2.12)–(2.13), distinct from L0,L1.

import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import LongTails.Template

open Set
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.CompositeGeneralizedSmooth

open OracleTemplate

structure Public where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  L0 : ℝ
  L1 : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.linearE Public.completeE

structure Params extends Public where
  G : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

inductive Query (p : Public) where
  | gradient (x : p.E)
  | prox (a : ℝ) (z v : p.E)

structure Instance (p : Public) where
  f : p.E → ℝ
  ψ : p.E → ℝ
  Q : Set p.E
  grad : p.E → p.E
  prox : ℝ → p.E → p.E → p.E

noncomputable def objective {p : Public} (I : Instance p) (x : p.E) : ℝ := I.f x + I.ψ x

noncomputable def proxObjective {p : Public} (I : Instance p) (a : ℝ) (z v u : p.E) : ℝ :=
  ‖u - z‖ ^ 2 / (2 * a) + ⟪v, u - z⟫ + I.ψ u

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance := Instance
  Query := Query
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid q := 0 < q.L0 ∧ 0 ≤ q.L1 ∧ 0 < q.R ∧ 0 < q.Δ ∧ 0 ≤ q.G ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q I oracle :=
    (∀ k seed x, oracle.answer k (0, .gradient x) seed = I.grad x) ∧
    (∀ k seed a z v, oracle.answer k (0, .prox a z v) seed = I.prox a z v) ∧
    ConvexOn ℝ univ I.f ∧
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt I.f (I.grad x) x) ∧
    Continuous I.grad ∧
    (∀ x y M, (∀ θ ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ‖I.grad (x + θ • (y - x))‖ ≤ M) →
      ‖I.grad x - I.grad y‖ ≤ (q.L0 + q.L1 * M) * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    Convex ℝ I.Q ∧
    ConvexOn ℝ I.Q I.ψ ∧
    (∀ a, 0 < a → ∀ z v, I.prox a z v ∈ I.Q ∧
      IsMinOn (proxObjective I a z v) I.Q (I.prox a z v)) ∧
    q.x0 ∈ I.Q ∧
    (∃ xstar ∈ I.Q, IsMinOn (objective I) I.Q xstar ∧ ‖q.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ q.R ∧
      objective I q.x0 - objective I xstar ≤ q.Δ ∧ ‖I.grad xstar‖ ≤ q.G)
  successful q I output P :=
    ∃ xstar ∈ I.Q, IsMinOn (objective I) I.Q xstar ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _),
        output ω ∈ I.Q ∧ objective I (output ω) - objective I xstar ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.CompositeGeneralizedSmooth
